claude.sample_unit: ECGs (training); external validation 219,231 ECGs; consumer-device sets Apple Watch n=9835 and QOCA n=31,517
models_evaluated: Lead-I AI-ECG models trained on 12-lead-derived data, fine-tuned on Apple Watch and QOCA ECG102D recordings

links.outcome: AUC on consumer-device ECGs after fine-tuning on device-specific labeled data versus direct deployment
links.effect: Fine-tuning significantly improved AUCs across eight tasks for both devices (low EF 0.85/0.86; PASP 0.73/0.68; anemia 0.73/0.69); about 500-1000 labeled ECGs needed, smaller sets can be harmful.
links.quote: After fine-tuning, AUCs across eight classification tasks for the Apple Watch and QOCA ECG102D were significantly improved, with high performance for low EF (0.85/0.86) and more modest performance for elevated PASP (0.73/0.68) and anemia (0.73/0.69).

links.outcome: Accuracy loss from device and context domain shift when deploying to consumer single-lead ECGs
links.effect: Direct deployment to Apple Watch (n=9835) and QOCA ECG102D (n=31,517) produced substantial accuracy losses, whereas cross-hospital AUC decline was <0.03.
links.quote: In contrast, direct deployment to consumer ECGs from Apple Watch (n = 9835) and QOCA ECG102D (n = 31,517) produced substantial accuracy losses.

links.outcome: Performance variation across sites versus acquisition devices
links.effect: Cross-hospital validation showed minimal overall degradation (AUC decline <0.03), but consumer devices showed substantial accuracy losses.
links.quote: Cross-hospital validation showed minimal overall degradation (AUC decline <0.03).

links.outcome: Model performance across clinical subgroups by cardiac rhythm
links.effect: Performance was higher in sinus rhythm than in atrial fibrillation.
links.quote: Performance was higher in sinus rhythm than atrial fibrillation.

unlisted_practices: Releasing an evaluation-only dataset (HOME) for reproducible benchmarking of cross-device generalization
Determining minimum labeled sample size (learning curves) for reliable local fine-tuning

screen.practice: local fine-tuning/recalibration on target-device data before deployment
screen.reason: The study empirically assesses the impact of device-level domain shift (consumer single-lead vs clinical 12-lead) and tests the deployment practice of local calibration/fine-tuning using sample-size requirements to prevent performance degradation.

primary.practice: local fine-tuning for domain shift mitigation
